answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use a time-locked reputation escrow: every new identity first completes small public-goods tasks whose results stay openly auditable, so spinning up a hundred fakes means a hundred rounds of real work while an honest newcomer does just one, and the pigment of finished work grows in public while each task's thread is recorded for anyone to check and the onyx of the process is set so faking a history costs far more than any reward the fakes could collect.
